zotero.abstractNote: Discrete diffusion models have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models for language modeling. While their scaling behavior has been studied in the context of continuous data, it remains poorly understood for discrete data. In this work, we perform a systematic study of the scaling behavior of discrete diffusion language models. We find that, similar to autoregressive models, discrete diffusion models exhibit predictable scaling laws with respect to model size, dataset size, and compute. We further investigate the impact of the diffusion process and the discretization scheme on the scaling behavior. Our results suggest that discrete diffusion models can achieve performance competitive with autoregressive models at scale, while offering potential advantages in terms of generation speed and control.
